title: Paying for Televisions That Did Not Exist: Legend's First Deal
conflicts: Amount lost: Liu (PCWorld, 2009) said two-thirds of the 200,000 yuan; Ling Zhijun's history (via the Summaries.com summary) says RMB 140,000 on TVs that did not exist. Consistent, so both are given and attributed. Dollar value of the capital varies ($24,000 to $40,000) so only yuan is used. The slate's 1985 date for the deal is not given by English sources, which call it the first big deal after the late-1984 founding; approx_date 1984.
notes: English sources do not say who arranged the TV deal or name the swindler, so the loss is put on 'the company', not Liu. Ling names Wang Shuhe as first general manager; the story mentions him. The book itself was not available; a Summaries.com summary of it is cited, with all but the 140,000 figure, the guard-post detail and Wang Shuhe backed by other sources. Industry changed from software to computers. Stance affirms (Laozi ch. 71).
